messages:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-pool-highmem-us-west-2 queue growth detected. queued_requests=18240, avg_enqueue_ms=3200, 5xx_rate=2.1%, 429_rate spike. autoscaler: at max_replicas=12. suspect recent batching/cache config change. tagging oncall.
elaine (oncall): I see it, paging sam and priya now. Allocating incident channel. Anyone oncall handoff? :hand: Pagerduty says high priority customer impact (errors + latency).
sam: taking pager. I'm looking at metrics — prefix cache hit rate for highmem pool dropped from 92% -> 18% in last deploy. Continuous batching window_ms was rolled from 100 -> 10 in last config PR (env: prod). That would reduce batch sizes and raise token overhead.
priya: who rolled that change? I remember a quick perf tweak last night. If batch window shrank to 10ms we could be starving the GPUs with tiny batches. Also prefix cache eviction TTL was lowered in the same deploy (ttl=30s -> 5s).
matt: confirm logs show many prefix cache misses, KV cache thrash, and smaller effective batch lengths. Here's a snippet from the runtime logs showing 429s and small batch sizes:
```
[2026-03-14T09:12:02Z] pool=highmem shard=3 batch_size=2 latency_ms=420 avg_enqueue_ms=3100 resp_code=429
[2026-03-14T09:12:02Z] pool=highmem cache_prefix_hits=7 cache_prefix_misses=213
[2026-03-14T09:12:03Z] pool=highmem batch_size=1 latency_ms=620 resp_code=503
```
elaine (oncall): high customer impact — some enterprise customers seeing request timeouts and retries. Need immediate mitigations and a follow-up rollback. Priorities: 1) stop ongoing customer errors, 2) lift pressure so autoscaler can catch up, 3) capture postmortem data.
sam: immediate plan: (A) temporarily increase autoscaler max_replicas to 20 to buy capacity, (B) revert continuous_batching.window_ms to 100ms and restore prefix cache ttl to 90s, (C) add routing rule to send premium customers to dedicated pool if available. I'll run (A) and (B) now.
priya: I'll prepare a safe rollback PR for the config changes and coordinate with release to avoid flapping. Also will open a short-lived feature-flag to disable the aggressive batching change.
matt: applying scaling now:
```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/gpu-worker-highmem --replicas=20
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/pools/highmem/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" -d '{"continuous_batching.window_ms":100, "prefix_cache.ttl_seconds":90}'
```
sam: executed scale command, control-plane change submitted (200). autoscaler max_replicas bumped. seeing worker pods coming up.
elaine (oncall): monitor queue length and 429 rate. mark customer comms team to draft incident banner if impact persists. @pagerduty-bot please escalate to infra-leads if no stable condition in 10m.
pagerduty-bot: Escalation queued: infra-leads notified.
(3m pass) matt: early signal: queue length dropping from 18k -> 8k, 429_rate down ~60%. batch_size median rising from 2 -> 12. cache hit rate climbing to 55%.
sam: good. keep scaling until we see stable <500 queued requests while we finish rollback PR. Prioritize not to overshoot cost-wise — will set an autoscale cooldown.
priya: PR opened to revert the two config changes, linking to the deploy that introduced them. I'll request an expedited review and a canary rollback to a subset of traffic first. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/configs/pulls/9823
elaine (oncall): oncall handoff in 20m to priya. sam, if you need me beyond that ping separately. Also capture correlation with recent traffic spike — ruling out sudden customer burst first.
matt: added a temporary routing rule to divert 40% of premium-prod traffic to dedicated-highmem-1 pool to reduce tail latencies. Command: `redwoodctl route update --pool highmem --split 60,40 --alt-pool dedicated-highmem-1`
sam: monitoring: at +12m since mitigations started: queued_requests=420, avg_enqueue_ms=180, 429_rate ~0.2%. CPU/GPU utilization normalized. Looks like reverting batching + cache TTL + scale did it.
elaine (oncall): handing off to priya now for post-incident cleanup and postmortem. I will update incident channel and customer comms. Priya, you take lead for RCA and PROD revert timeline.
priya: taking over. Next steps: 1) finalize rollback canary and full revert, 2) audit CI guardrails for small batching windows, 3) add histogram alert for prefix_cache_hit_rate < 80% and sustained queue growth > 1k for 5m. I'll own the postmortem doc.
matt: quick note for postmortem: include kernel selection logs showing increased per-token compute due to small batches and the link to observability dashboard (https://dash.internal/highmem/queue).
priya: creating postmortem doc and will include timeline + mitigation commands + revert PR link. ETA for full revert: 30 minutes subject to canary health.
elaine (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll mark incident as mitigated once stable for 15m and will coordinate customer comms. :white_check_mark:
sam: thumbs — nice quick work. We'll follow up with a retro around config rollout process to avoid silent perf regressions.
priya: filing follow-ups: add gating tests (end-to-end latency + batch size distribution) and require config change sign-off from runtime oncall.
matt: leaving logs + metrics snapshots in the incident folder: s3://redwood-incidents/1785123456/metrics.tar.gz
elaine (oncall): incident closed -> mitigated at 1785124056. Postmortem owner: priya.
